name: Surveyor 1
title: The First Soft Touch
blurb: Before anyone dared to land, Surveyor 1 asked the Moon a simple question: will the ground hold? It did — proving lunar soil was firm and paving the way for Apollo.
log: They told me the Moon might swallow me whole, like quicksand made of dust.
But my three footpads touched down and the ground held. Firm. Quiet. Ready.
I sent home thousands of pictures so humans could see where to step next. Then the long lunar night fell — and I kept waiting.
sign: — Surveyor 1, signing off from the Ocean of Storms, 1966

stats.label: Soil strong enough to land on
U.S. soft landing on another world

condition.note: No wind, no rain, no rust. Only slow micrometeorite sandblasting and sunlight remain.

name: Apollo 11 Descent Stage
title: Left on the Porch
blurb: The gold-foil base of the Eagle. When two astronauts blasted home, the platform that carried them down stayed behind — untouched in a total vacuum.
log: Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed — and now, it is time to go home.
The ascent engine fires. Our legs, our ladder and our plaque stay behind on the porch.
“We came in peace for all mankind.” Please keep the light on for us.

stats.label: Experiments left running: seismic & laser mirror

condition.note: Without air to erode anything, the astronauts’ footprints may last millions of years.

name: Apollo 15 Lunar Rover
title: The First Car Off Earth
blurb: Folded like origami and driven across the Moon on wire-mesh tires, the rover carried astronauts miles beyond walking range. It is still parked at Hadley Rille.
log: Seat belts on. Battery full. Wheels woven from wire, ready to roll.
We rolled beside a canyon older than any mountain on Earth, and found a rock that remembers the Moon’s birth.
Now I’m parked facing the rille, keys left in. Whenever someone comes back, I’ll be right here.

condition.note: Its batteries died ages ago, but the frame and tires are likely just as they were left.

name: Sojourner / Pathfinder
title: The Microwave-Sized Pioneer
blurb: A 23-pound rover the size of a microwave oven that proved wheels work on Mars — and started a whole lineage of robotic explorers.
log: Hello, Mars! I’m small, but my six wheels are brave.
I sniffed rocks with my chemistry sensor and never wandered far from my lander — it was my lifeline home.
Then our last message came. I stayed beside Pathfinder on the red plain, a tiny explorer who showed the way for giants.

condition.note: Resting beside its lander in Ares Vallis, slowly turning the colour of the Martian plain.

name: Opportunity Rover (Oppy)
title: The 90-Day Miracle
blurb: Built for 90 days, Oppy ran for 15 years and 28 miles — until the global dust storm of 2018 blotted out the sun.
log: The sky is turning dark, and my battery is running low.
I have rolled farther than anyone thought possible, and I found proof that water once flowed here.
My solar panels can’t see the Sun anymore. It’s okay — it was a wonderful drive. Thank you for every single day.

condition.note: Declared complete in February 2019 after over a thousand recovery commands went unanswered.

name: InSight Lander
title: The Martian Heartbeat
blurb: InSight put a stethoscope to Mars. It heard over 1,300 marsquakes until its solar arrays were choked by red dust.
log: I listened to Mars breathe — thump, rumble, tremor. A whole planet, alive with echoes.
Now the dust has settled on my wings and my power is nearly gone. I’m okay. I have heard what I came here to hear.
Don’t worry about me. Keep listening to the worlds beyond.

condition.note: It tipped its arrays to shed dust, but the Martian wind never swept them fully clean.
